transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Maya Ortiz (Stratus Head of ML), Jonas Becker (Stratus Platform), Samir Patel (Stratus Security), Ellen Wu (Stratus PM)
---
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is the Stratus weekly, quick check-in on the KV synthesis work. Priya and I are here, Diego as well. Maya you want to kick off with the latest from your side?
[00:18] Maya Ortiz: Yeah thanks Alex. Quick note we've run two short warmups since last week, one with the naive TTLs and one with the cohort-driven TTLs that Priya suggested. I put the results into the sheet we shared, um the file is linked in the deck — /sheets/stratus-kv-results-20271208.
[00:33] Priya Nair: Nice. So the baseline run last Tuesday showed global KV hit about 18%, prefix reuse around 9% for long-tail queries. After cohort TTL adjustments and bumping prefetch cadence to 200ms window we saw KV hit jump to roughly 57% for our high-frequency cohorts but long-tail cohorts stayed low.
[00:54] Jonas Becker: Quick clarification, when you say high-frequency cohorts that's top 5% of sessions by traffic right? 
[01:02] Priya Nair: Correct, top 5% by request volume. Those sessions are heavily skewed to the same few prefixes, so prefix reuse and KV benefit a lot.
[01:10] Samir Patel: From security perspective, two things: first we need to confirm where keys live — our compliance team requires KMS in eu-west-1 for EU data. Second, audit logs for inference calls need 12 months retention. Do you have a doc for that?
[01:26] Alex Chen: Yep we'll attach the Security pack and SOC2 artifacts. Priya, we'll also surface the KMS options in the private deploy checklist — is that in the cloud-config doc?
[01:36] Priya Nair: It's in the private deploy notes, but I'll send a short summary. For hosted we have KMS integrations but region constraints vary; for Private you can bring your own KMS.
[01:47] Ellen Wu: On the warmup runs — we're seeing a big variance in cold start misses during peak hour. Is that eviction-related or an artifact of sequence-length differences?
[01:58] Priya Nair: Good question. A couple causes: eviction pressure during bursts when our prefetch cadence didn't keep up, and prompt variation where user prompts include session-specific tokens leading to less prefix canonicalization.
[02:10] Maya Ortiz: Right, we noticed a lot of prompt noise — users append ephemeral IDs to every prompt, so the prefix is slightly different each time. We tried a lightweight normalizer but it's brittle.
[02:22] Alex Chen: That ties into prompt-reuse strategy — we can canonicalize certain tracked fields, and also send a pre-hash of the canonical prefix to Redwood to improve matching. There's a tradeoff of engineering overhead vs hit-rate gains.
[02:35] Jonas Becker: Can you explain session-snapshotting again? We heard that in the last SE doc but want to make sure we implement it correctly.
[02:43] Priya Nair: Sure. Session-snapshotting is a small client-side hook that captures the session's last N prompts and metadata and sends it as an opaque blob to an analysis endpoint. Redwood can then replay and compute exact KV keys that should've hit and where mismatches happened. Low perf overhead, but we can capture the divergence patterns.
[03:00] Jonas Becker: Ok, we'll add that to staging.
[03:04] Diego Ramos: One practical ask — when you run the 24-hour warmup, can you keep a concurrent trace on Redwood's side so we can correlate misses to evictions? We want to see slot occupancy over time.
[03:16] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll run a live trace capture — need you to confirm a window when you ramp traffic.
[03:23] Maya Ortiz: Next Wed afternoon works.
[03:26] Priya Nair: Noted.
[03:28] [04:00] (sketch: group cross talk about numbers and artifacts)
[04:12] Alex Chen: Let's go over numbers in the sheet — Maya, can you summarise week-over-week delta?
[04:20] Maya Ortiz: Sure. Baseline run: total token throughput small, KV hit 18%, token-level cost estimate $0.55 per 1k tokens with lots of model repeats. After cohort TTL + prefetch: KV hit 57% for top cohorts, overall KV hit 38% across all cohorts. Latency improved 30% p50, cost estimate dropped about 22% in that run. But a second run with a slightly different traffic shape dropped overall hit to 33% — so sensitivity to traffic mix is high.
[04:55] Priya Nair: Right and that sensitivity suggests we need persistent warmup (24h) to get steady-state cache population and also better cohort segmentation — small cohorts with high churn should have shorter TTLs to avoid wasteful occupancy.
[05:08] Jonas Becker: What's the memory/slot impact on the serving nodes when TTLs are longer? We worried about OOM.
[05:15] Priya Nair: TTLs do increase occupancy, but our recommendation is to cap per-slot reserved cache for cohort entries and have an eviction thermostat: LRU within cohort with proportional eviction when overall mem crosses threshold. We can show a run with reserved buckets.
[05:27] Alex Chen: We also tested prefix coalescing in a small experiment — combining similar prompts into canonical forms before keying. It reduced key fragmentation but missed when prompt semantics changed. The tradeoff is false positives in reuse vs bigger hit-rate gains.
[05:41] Ellen Wu: Did you see any hallucination or quality regressions from coalescing?
[05:46] Priya Nair: So far no quality regressions on small evals, but it's model-dependent. We recommend A/B and some eval prompt sets to detect regressions. Redwood Optimize can run evaluation hooks on these rollouts.
[05:59] [06:15] (brief pause; someone shares link in chat)
[06:22] Maya Ortiz: A couple more anomalies — during the evening spike last Thursday, we saw a sudden drop in KV hits from 62% to 21% momentarily. Logs show a redeploy around the same time, maybe state not warmed.
[06:36] Priya Nair: Redeploys will bust local caches; if you don't use persistent snapshotting or shared cache across pods you'll see that. For Dedicated we can pin instances with session affinity, or use session-snapshot resume to rebuild quickly.
[06:49] Jonas Becker: How viable is shared cache for us? Our infra is on GCE and we have some constraints on cross-zone network egress.
[06:59] Priya Nair: Shared cache adds network overhead; for low-latency needs Dedicated local caches with session affinity are often better. If you have cross-zone egress limits, we recommend local per-cluster caches with smart prefetching and longer warmup windows.
[07:13] Samir Patel: Back to security — in private deploy we need KMS in eu-west-1 and all audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Can Redwood support S3 forwarding + KMS envelope?
[07:25] Alex Chen: Yes, we support S3 + KMS envelope options for logs; we'll drop the integration doc. Priya can confirm exact retention windows we can support in hosted vs private.
[07:37] Priya Nair: Hosted has configurable retention tiers (30/90/365 days with add-on). Private you control retention.
[07:45] Maya Ortiz: Great. On the cost question, Alex, you mentioned a new estimate assuming 38% overall KV hit — can you walk through numbers?
[07:54] Alex Chen: Sure off the top — rough calc in the spreadsheet: with 38% hit, token cost drops around 20% because hot tokens avoid model compute; p50 latency ~ -25%. If you go to Dedicated and sustain a 50% hit with affinity, unit cost drops further but you'll have committed spend. We'll share both commissioned and on-demand scenarios.
[08:17] Jonas Becker: For the dedicated config, are there autoscaling options during spikes? We can't have fixed capacity always.
[08:24] Priya Nair: Dedicated supports autoscale policies with burst capacity lanes; the cache warmup is a bit trickier during scale-out because new nodes start cold — we recommend keeping a small warm pool and using session-snapshot resume for rapid refill.
[08:37] [09:00] (audio glitch for a few seconds)
[09:12] Alex Chen: Let's talk about next diagnostic steps. Priya?
[09:15] Priya Nair: Diagnostic plan: 1) Run 24h continuous warmup with cohort TTLs and adaptive prefetch, maintain live trace; 2) deploy session-snapshot hook in staging to capture per-session divergence; 3) run synthetic 100k session perf run to correlate eviction events; 4) rerun cost sheet with observed hit rates. We'll own 1 and 2 with Stratus helping on traffic generation.
[09:41] Maya Ortiz: That sounds good. On item 1 we need Redwood to also share a low-level trace with eviction and slot occupancy.
[09:49] Priya Nair: We'll provide that; need the staging window.
[09:53] Jonas Becker: We'll block next Wed 13:00-16:00 UTC.
[09:57] Alex Chen: Great. Any blockers for the team? Samir?
[10:02] Samir Patel: The only blocker is if hosted can't guarantee KMS eu-west-1 or the exact audit retention — we may need Private for that. We'll confirm after reading the doc.
[10:12] Alex Chen: Understood; we'll surface PKI and KMS options.
[10:15] Ellen Wu: Quick question — for canonicalization, do you provide a library or do we build our own?
[10:20] Priya Nair: Redwood provides a small canonicalizer helper in the SDK that does field scrubbing and pre-hash generation, but for app-specific tokens you'll need a small local preprocessor. We can share examples.
[10:31] Maya Ortiz: Please share example code.
[10:33] Alex Chen: Will do. Priya, anything else?
[10:36] Priya Nair: One more note — we saw a category of misses caused by prompt templates that include variable orderings; for those we saw benefit by order-normalizing placeholders. Might be a low-effort win.
[10:48] Jonas Becker: We'll add that to the staging normalizer test.
[10:52] [11:00] (wrap-up)
[11:04] Alex Chen: Recap: 24h warmup + live trace, session-snapshotting in staging, 100k synthetic run next Tue, Alex to send updated pricing and docs, Samir to confirm KMS/audit needs. We'll reconvene same time next week.
[11:20] Maya Ortiz: Thanks all.
[11:22] Diego Ramos: Thanks team — I'll follow up in CRM with notes.
[11:25] (call ends)
